content: A tongue cleaner, also known as a tongue scraper, is a specialized oral hygiene tool designed to remove bacterial buildup, food debris, fungi, and dead cells from the surface of the tongue. The bacteria and fungi that accumulate on the tongue are associated with various oral health and general health issues. Additionally, decaying bacteria on the rear of the tongue produce volatile sulfur compounds, which are the primary cause of halitosis, or bad breath. Tongue cleaners effectively lift and remove these materials from the tongue's surface. Ergonomically designed tongue cleaners are shaped to match the anatomy of the tongue and are optimized to lift and trap the plaque coating, ensuring effective cleaning of the tongue's surface. They are available in various materials, including plastic, metal, and wood. The effectiveness of these devices depends on their shape, dimensions, configuration, and the quality of the contact surfaces and materials used. Historically, tongue cleaning has been practiced since ancient times in India and China. In Ayurveda, the traditional Indian system of medicine, tongue cleaning is recommended as part of a daily hygiene regimen to remove toxic debris, referred to as Ama. In the 19th century, tongue cleaners were commonly made from materials such as sterling silver, ivory, and tortoiseshell. Tongue cleaning is essential for maintaining fresh breath. It helps remove millions of bacteria (up to 500 different types), decaying food particles, fungi (such as Candida), and dead cells from the rear surface of the tongue. Scientific studies indicate that in 80-90% of cases, bad breath originates in the oral cavity, primarily from material on the rear of the tongue. Only 10-20% of cases are linked to the stomach or tonsils. Tongue cleaning also contributes to better oral hygiene. Approximately 70% of the bacteria in the oral cavity reside on the tongue's surface. These microorganisms thrive on protein-rich areas of the tongue, derived from decaying food particles, and can spread to other areas of the mouth, including the teeth and gums. This bacterial spread significantly contributes to periodontal problems, plaque formation, tooth decay, gum infections, and gum recession. Oral bacteria are also linked to several serious systemic infections, including cardiovascular issues (such as heart attacks and strokes), pneumonia caused by inhaling oral bacteria, premature birth and low birth weight in newborns, and an increased risk of complications in diabetic patients. In alternative medicine, tongue cleaning is believed to provide a reflexogenic massage to different areas of the tongue, as recognized in traditional Chinese medicine. It also enhances the sense of taste by cleaning the taste buds and stimulates the secretion of digestive enzymes. In recent years, the medical and dental communities, including dentists and hygienists, have increasingly recommended daily tongue cleaning as part of general body hygiene, alongside tooth brushing and flossing. Tongue cleaning not only promotes overall health but also serves as an effective solution for bad breath. It is a healthy daily habit that supports self-esteem and personal image for those who adopt it.
